role: Main-actor wrapper around one UIApplication.beginBackgroundTask assertion that guarantees endBackgroundTask is called exactly once, either by the work's own end() or by the expiration handler; the handler holds the identifier token strongly, so the task is ended at expiry even if the owner dropped the assertion without end().
types: BackgroundTaskAssertion: class (@MainActor final) — owns one BackgroundTaskToken
BackgroundTaskToken: private class (@MainActor final) — holds the UIBackgroundTaskIdentifier, shared with the expiration handler
state: token: BackgroundTaskToken (instance; also captured strongly by the expiration handler)

units.does: Begins a named UIKit background task, storing its identifier in the token; the expiration handler (main thread, assumed MainActor) holds the token strongly, logs a warning via debugLog, runs the caller's onExpire (e.g. MorningProcessingService sets skipSleepWait) and then ends the task through the token, whether or not the assertion object is still alive.
calls: closure:onExpire supplied by MorningProcessingService.processOvernightData (sets skipSleepWait = true) or the default no-op from WorkoutRecorder stop / EmuquApp auto-archive

flags.text: No test in EmuquTests references BackgroundTaskAssertion; the exactly-once end() contract (expiry then completion, or the reverse) that keeps iOS from killing the app is unverified.

units.does: Ends the background task through the token (no-op when already ended).
units.entry: Called by the owner's `defer` (MorningProcessingService, WorkoutRecorder+Stop, EmuquApp.autoArchivePendingSession).

units.does: Ends the background task if one is held and resets the identifier to .invalid; a second call is a no-op.
units.entry: Called by BackgroundTaskAssertion.end() and by the iOS expiration handler installed in BackgroundTaskAssertion.init.

branches.effect: true: return without calling UIKit; false: call endBackgroundTask and set .invalid.
